Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the audit/logs evidence you requested for FinCo Bank's security review:

- Example export of audit logs showing "who accessed what/when" (user/service identity, action, resource, timestamp)

- Clarification on retention defaults and configurable retention windows
- PII handling (redaction/encryption in logs) and data residency info

What we'll deliver next: 
1) A sample CSV (attached: audit_logs_sample.csv) with synthetic rows matching your schema request.
2) A short playbook (attach: redwood_audit_playbook.pdf) describing fields, export steps, and evidence artifacts we can provide (signed export manifest, access audit).
3) Confirmation of retention windows and a note about Dedicated/Private options for longer retention or on-prem storage.

Can you confirm the exact fields your compliance team needs (e.g., IP, request_id, user_id, model_name, prompt_hash)? If you prefer, we can package a full evidence export (logs + statement) and upload to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket.

I'll loop in our security and infra leads for the detailed answers — cc'd Sean and Aditya.

Next step: are you available for a 30-min follow-up on Thursday 18 Jun to walk the playbook and export sample?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good as a starting point. A few clarifications from our security team: 

- Schema: please include the request_id, timestamp (UTC), internal_user_id, external_user_id (if any), action (read/write/export), resource_path/model_name, IP address, and whether the request included PII.
- Delivery: S3 upload is preferred (we can provide a short-lived write role).
- Retention: our baseline ask is proof of retention policy plus a 12-month export of audit activity for the pilot environment. Is that feasible on hosted? If not, what would Dedicated/Private options look like?
- Evidence: we need a signed statement or chain-of-custody doc and a list of Redwoods staff who can access raw logs.

Can Sean or Aditya confirm whether IP addresses and request bodies are present in the logs and whether we can produce an export that redacts PII fields while preserving request_id and timestamps?

John

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 10:05 AM John Lee <john.lee@fincobank.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — this looks good as a starting point. A few clarifications from our security team: 
> 
> - Schema: please include the request_id, timestamp (UTC), internal_user_id, external_user_id (if any), action (read/write/export), resource_path/model_name, IP address, and whether the request included PII.
> - Delivery: S3 upload is preferred (we can provide a short-lived write role).
> - Retention: our baseline ask is proof of retention policy plus a 12-month export of audit activity for the pilot environment. Is that feasible on hosted? If not, what would Dedicated/Private options look like?
> - Evidence: we need a signed statement or chain-of-custody doc and a list of Redwoods staff who can access raw logs.
> 
> Thanks — tagging our infra/security folks to answer the technical bits. Quick answers below and more detail from Sean/Aditya to follow.
> 
> - Exports & formats: We can export logs as CSV or newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Exports can be delivered to an S3 bucket you provide via short-lived creds or via a secure HTTPS download link. The sample attached (audit_logs_sample.csv) shows a synthetic header.
> - IP & request metadata: IP addresses, request_id, model_name, and token-level consumption are present in our audit logs for hosted API calls. We can include those fields in exports.
> - PII handling: Our logs do not store plaintext prompts by default for hosted API; prompt content is redacted unless you enable request recording. We tag requests that include PII (simple boolean) and can run a redaction pipeline to remove or hash specified fields prior to export.
> - Retention: Hosted default retention for audit logs is 90 days. For the pilot / compliance evidence package we can produce a one-time 12-month export from archived indices if the data is available — there may be a charge and a short lead time. Dedicated customers can configure longer retention or ship logs to customer-managed storage for indefinite retention. Private deployments can keep everything on-prem under your control.
> - Internal access: Access to raw logs is restricted to specific roles (Site Reliability, Security on-call, and a small set of Platform Engineers). We will provide a named list and SCIM-backed groups for access control.
> 
> Sean/Aditya — can you confirm the exact CSV header we should provide and an estimate for producing a full 12-month export (cost + ETA)?
> 
> Thanks,
> Marissa

- Field completeness: will the export include HTTP headers (for IP provenance), user agent, and any service principal or API key id used?
- Redaction audit: when you run the redaction pipeline, can you provide a diff/audit of what was redacted (hashes + original field name) as part of the evidence package?
- Timeline: can you provide an ETA for the full evidence package and an example of the signed statement / chain-of-custody doc?

If you can provide sample headers and a short timeline (hours/days) we can align with our compliance review.

Anna / John —

Thanks — answers below, and a proposed next step. Apologies for the slightly longer reply, pulled in the infra details.

1) Queryability & filtering: export jobs support time-range filters and arbitrary filters on request_id, user_id, resource_path, and model_name. You can request either a full export or a scoped export (e.g., all activity for model X between dates Y and Z).

2) Field completeness (typical CSV header): request_id,timestamp_utc,internal_user_id,external_user_id,action,resource_path,model_name,ip_address,http_headers,user_agent,pii_flag,prompt_hash,token_count
- http_headers is stored as a JSON string in the CSV cell by default; we can expand to discrete columns if preferred.

3) Redaction audit: when we run the redaction pipeline we produce a manifest (redaction_manifest.json) listing original_field_name -> redaction_hash and a checksum. For evidence we provide the manifest plus a signed statement (sample in the attached redwood_audit_playbook.pdf) and a chain-of-custody log that shows who exported the file and when.

4) Timeline & cost: 
- Scoped export (up to 30 days): typically 24 hours turnaround.
- Large export (12 months): estimate 3-5 business days and an ad-hoc export fee (I will get precise numbers from Billing).

5) Named access: current Redwood staff with raw log access: Sean Gallagher (Security Lead), Ravi Sharma (Platform Eng), Aditya Rao (Infra). We will provide a SCIM group and export an access list for your records.

Deliverables we can prepare this week:
- audit_logs_export_20260620.zip (ndjson + CSV + redaction_manifest + signed statement) — will upload to your S3 if you share a write role.
- redwood_audit_playbook.pdf (attached)

Next step: Can we schedule a 30-min evidence handoff on Mon 22 Jun at 10:00 AM ET? If S3 creds are easier, please send the short-lived role and target bucket and we will start the export.

Thanks,
Marissa
